fi-pethia-conchonius.title: Rosy Barb
fi-pethia-conchonius.summary: The rosy barb, Pethia conchonius, is a small cyprinid found from Pakistan throughout India, Nepal and Bangladesh. Generally considered one of the hardiest small cyprinids in the hobby, it is an…
rows: schooling species by nature and ideally should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Omnivore. Studies have shown it to be a generalised omnivore feeding on worms, insects and other small invertebrates, as well as plant material and organic detritus.
Described from 'Ponds of northeastern Bengal; Kosi and Ami rivers, India' but according to current knowledge is extensively distributed from Pakistan throughout India, Nepal , and Bangladesh .
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a heavily-planted set-up with a dark substrate.
The addition of some floating plants and driftwood roots or branches to diffuse the light entering the tank also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-puntigrus-tetrazona.title: Tiger Barb
fi-puntigrus-tetrazona.summary: The tiger barb, Puntigrus tetrazona, is a small cyprinid probably endemic to central and southern Sumatra, Indonesia. Among the most ubiquitous species in the aquarium trade, it is seen mostly as…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Omnivore. Probably an omnivore feeding primarily on aquatic invertebrates, as well as smaller amounts of plant material and organic detritus in nature.
Probably endemic to central and southern Sumatra , with records from Borneo corresponding to congeners.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a well-decorated set-up.
The addition of floating or overhanging vegetation and driftwood roots or branches also seems to be appreciated.

fi-puntius-titteya.title: Cherry Barb
fi-puntius-titteya.summary: The cherry barb, Puntius titteya, is a small cyprinid endemic to the Kelani and Nilwala river basins in the southwestern 'wet zone' of Sri Lanka. Among the most ubiquitous small cyprinids in the…
rows: schooling species by nature, and at least 6-10 specimens should be purchased.
Wild fish are probably foragers feeding on diatoms, algae, organic detritus, small insects, worms, crustaceans, and other zooplankton.
Endemic to Sri Lanka where it is restricted to the Kelani and Nilwala river basins in the southwestern 'wet zone' of the island, plus smaller drainages in the area between them.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a heavily-planted set-up with a dark substrate.
The addition of some floating plants, driftwood roots or branches, and leaf litter also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-pethia-padamya.title: Odessa Barb
fi-pethia-padamya.summary: The Odessa barb, Pethia padamya, is a small cyprinid from central Myanmar, also recorded from the lower Chindwin, a tributary of the Ayeyarwady. In the trade since the early 1970s, it first appeared…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Likely to be a foraging omnivore feeding on worms, insects and other small invertebrates, as well as plant material and organic detritus.
Known only from central Myanmar where the type specimens were collected from a man-made pond fed by a small stream in a village called Toe Gyi which lies in the administrative division of Mandalay.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a heavily-planted set-up with a dark substrate.
The addition of some floating plants and driftwood roots or branches to diffuse the light entering the tank also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.

fi-puntius-semifasciolatus.title: Koi Gold Barb
fi-puntius-semifasciolatus.summary: Barbodes semifasciolatus, the green or Chinese barb, is a cyprinid from Vietnam, Taiwan, southwestern China and northern Laos. The natural green form is an infrequent find in the trade, but the…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security, and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. A foraging omnivore feeding mostly on benthic diatoms, algae, organic detritus, small insects, worms, crustaceans, and other zooplankton in nature.
Occurs throughout Vietnam , Taiwan , and southwestern China and northern Laos, and has also been recorded in Russia though it's unclear whether the latter population is naturally-occurring or not.
notes: The golden form (see 'Notes') is among the hardier, most undemanding species available in the aquarium hobby and as such is a good choice for beginners.
Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a heavily-planted set-up with a dark substrate.

fi-dawkinsia-filamentosa.title: Filamentosus Barb
fi-dawkinsia-filamentosa.summary: The filament barb, Dawkinsia filamentosa, is a cyprinid endemic to the Western Ghats region of southern India, in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Adult males and some females develop filament-like…
rows: schooling species by nature so ideally 8-10 specimens should be purchased.
Omnivore. Probably a foraging omnivore feeding on a variety of worms, insects, crustaceans, plant material, and other organic debris in nature.
Endemic to but widespread within the Western Ghats mountains region of southern India in the states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, and possibly restricted to the south of the latter.
notes: Not difficult to keep in a well-maintained set-up, though we recommend aquascaping the tank to resemble a flowing stream or river with a substrate of variably-sized, water-worn rocks, sand, fine gravel and perhaps some small boulders.

This can be further furnished with driftwood roots or branches, and while the majority of aquatic plants will fail to thrive in such surroundings hardy types such as Microsorum , Bolbitis or Anubias spp.

fi-eirmotus-octozona.title: Eight Striped Barb
fi-eirmotus-octozona.summary: Eirmotus octozona is a small cyprinid with eight dark body bars, known from Johor state in Peninsular Malaysia. The type series came from aquarium fish said to originate at Bueng Boraphet in…
rows: shoaling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Predator / carnivore. Likely to feed on small invertebrates, algae and other zooplankton in nature.
The type series consisted of aquarium specimens apparently originated from a lake named Bueng Boraphet in western Thailand , but despite extensive sampling of the region in the…
notes: Will thrive in a heavily-planted or forest stream-type set-up, the latter comprising a soft substrate, dim lighting, roots, branches and leaf litter as décor.
You could also add aquatic plants that can survive under such conditions such as Microsorum , Taxiphyllum or Cryptocoryne spp.

fi-haludaria-fasciata.title: Red Panda Barb
fi-haludaria-fasciata.summary: The melon barb, Haludaria fasciata, is a small cyprinid endemic to the Western Ghats of southern India, in Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. It exists in a number of colour forms, and it is…
rows: group of at least 8-10 specimens, include other schooling fishes to provide security and you'll be rewarded with a more natural-looking spectacle.
Omnivore. Wild fish are foraging omnivores feeding on diatoms, algae, organic detritus, small insects, worms, crustaceans, and other zooplankton.
Endemic to the Western Ghats mountains in the south Indian states of Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu where it ranges from Kanyakumari district at the southern tip of the…
notes: Fairly undemanding provided the aquarium is well-maintained but can appear a little washed out in very sparsely decorated set-ups.

A combination of subdued lighting and a dark substrate will encourage it to show its best colours, and it can look superb in a planted set-up decorated with pieces of bogwood, twisted roots and patches of floating vegetation.
